notes: Derived edit without worlds. The premise 143 = 11 × 13 is the class ProductOfTwoSmallerWholeNumbers (a product of two smaller whole numbers greater than 1; DL has no multiplication); the definition of composite is firm. The factorization is the one premise that can give way, so it is the top-level gives_up; the record states this in its notes, its premise queries' chains and its determinacy_why. q0 (a product of two smaller whole numbers greater than 1), q2 (tiling a rectangle, a firm equivalent class) and q1 (divisible by 11) need no arithmetic once the factorization 143 = 11 × 13 is a stored belief: the factorization item now holds the product class and the divisibility by 11 and 13, which give way together; a prime's only divisor besides itself is 1 (firm rule; divides is irreflexive). Relabelled dl (theory arithmetic dropped) on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check. q3 (more than two divisors, 2026-10-31) goes through the RELATIONS.md chain instance_of ∘ subclass_of ⊑ instance_of: primes have exactly two divisors, composites more than two (firm classes, disjoint); the old q3 conjunction moved to the propositional query type.

bridge_refs.tiles_def: A number of identical square tiles can fill a rectangle with at least two rows and at least two columns exactly when the number is a product of two whole numbers greater than 1.
bridge_refs.prime_two: Every prime number has exactly two positive divisors.

fol.notes: The factorization is a belief: times is uninterpreted, since built-in 11 * 13 == 143 could not give way. It is the one premise that gives way (top-level gives_up, as in the DL file). The rules are instances for 143 (finite quantifiers). 'A product of two whole numbers greater than 1' (tiling) is the same predicate as a product of two smaller ones: a factor greater than 1 of n is smaller than n.

times_def.says: If n = a × b, a and b divide n, and if also 1 < a, b < n, n is a product of two smaller whole numbers greater than 1.
times_def.z3: All([a, b], [(11, 13)], Implies(times(a, b) == 143, divides(a, 143) and divides(b, 143) and (Implies(1 < a and a < 143 and 1 < b and b < 143, product_of_smaller(143)))))

composite_def.says: A whole number greater than 1 that is the product of two smaller whole numbers greater than 1 is composite, not prime.

prime_def.says: A prime number has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

tiles.says: A number of identical square tiles can fill a rectangle with at least two rows and at least two columns exactly when the number is a product of two whole numbers greater than 1.

local.times: Int × Int product as the model believes it (ATTRIBUTES lists times as real; here on whole numbers)
